findings.what: The new run-count bound is pinned only by a 0x7FFFFFFF fixture, so its TIGHTNESS is unconstrained -- the same gap the author closed for the segment count in this round by adding aSegmentCountOnlyMODESTLYTooLargeIsAlsoRefused, and did not close for the run count. Measured in a copy of the staged bytes: replacing `runCount > c.remaining()` with `runCount > (long) c.remaining() * 100000` leaves :format:test, :ingest:test and :sequencer:test all green.
findings.failure_scenario: A later refactor loosens or rewrites the run bound (a multiplier, `a.length`, or a cast that widens it) while keeping it non-trivial. Every suite stays green because the only run-count fixture claims 0x7FFFFFFF, which any of those forms still rejects. A modestly corrupt v0 delta -- the shape a torn PUT actually produces -- then claims a few hundred thousand runs in a short object and sizes an ArrayList from it before reading a byte, restoring the allocation-from-a-count class this commit exists to close, on the v0 path every bucket already holds. A second fixture with a modest overclaim (say 9 runs in 8 remaining bytes, mirroring the segment-count test) would kill it.
